title: Teaching Philosophy
summary: I connect computer science foundations with responsible AI, healthcare computing, and trustworthy digital systems through research-informed teaching and practical learning.

pillars.name: Research-Informed, Practice-Driven
pillars.text: I connect core computer science with published examples from AI/ML, healthcare informatics, blockchain, and secure cloud systems, while preserving the breadth of the documented course portfolio.

pillars.name: AI/ML as Amplifier
pillars.text: Students learn to design and evaluate models responsibly—using AI/ML to augment insight, automate analysis, and generate ideas, while understanding limitations, bias, and reproducibility.

pillars.name: Mastery in Communication
pillars.text: I train students to write clearly and publish credibly: LaTeX proficiency, sound citation practice, and persuasive technical storytelling—because ideas must travel to matter.

pillars.name: Ethics, Security, and Impact
pillars.text: Privacy, explainability, fairness, and security provide a framework for discussing AI and healthcare applications, including the distinction between experimental models and validated clinical tools.

pillars.name: Learning by Building
pillars.text: Project-based learning, peer review, and iterative design cultivate autonomy and resilience. Students build artifacts—code, reports, demos—that demonstrate real capability.

callout: Graduates leave not only with skills but with habits: curiosity, clarity, and care.
